title: TicketState
description: Compiled ticket state as emitted by `rebar show <id>` (and the library show_ticket / MCP show_ticket tool), and the element shape of `list` / `search`. This is replay-derived state, not an event. Unknown properties are allowed so the event-sourced shape can evolve without breaking consumers. Shared sub-objects (comment/dep/file_impact_entry/verify_command_entry) are $ref'd from common.schema.json.

ticket_id.description: Canonical ticket id (the directory name on the tickets branch).

bridge_project.description: Tri-state Jira bridge target project key: null = absent/legacy (never declared), "" = explicit never-sync, "REB" (etc.) = sync target. Promote-only via edit once the ticket holds a binding.

repos.description: Repositories this ticket's work spans (freely editable).

inbound_deps.description: Computed inbound edges (read-time derivation, never persisted): every other ticket whose stored LINK targets this one, each entry meaning 'from_id <relation> this ticket', with the source ticket's current status. Present on the per-ticket show surfaces (CLI show default view, library show_ticket(include_inbound=True), MCP show_ticket); omitted from list/search projections.

plan_review_health.description: Detailed-only, read-time plan-review health computed from the certified attestation. It is never persisted in ticket events and is omitted from ordinary list/search projections. The unavailable variant is compact and exact; available variants remain extensible.

attestations.description: Kind-keyed map of cryptographic attestation records (epic dark-acme-lumen): each key is an attestation kind (e.g. 'plan-review', 'completion-verifier') and each value is a signature record {manifest, algorithm, key_id, head_sha, signed_at, author} (the raw HMAC hex is stripped from public output). Additive across kinds, last-writer-wins within a kind, so independent gate attestations coexist instead of clobbering one slot. Omitted when the ticket has no attestations. The legacy top-level `signature` field is a back-compat mirror of the most-recent attestation.

last_reopened_at.description: ns-epoch timestamp of the most recent closed->open (reopen) transition; absent/null if the ticket was never reopened. Read by validity-on-read to invalidate an attestation signed before a reopen.

source_id.description: Provenance (P1.2 import): the ticket's original id in the source store. Present only on tickets created by `rebar import`.

source_created_at.description: Provenance (P1.2 import): the ticket's original creation timestamp (ns) in the source store. The local CREATE event uses a fresh HLC timestamp; this preserves the original for reporting/migration.

source_author.description: Provenance (P1.2 import): the ticket's original author in the source store.

source_env.description: Provenance (P1.2 import): the ticket's original environment id in the source store.

creation_channel.description: The public ingress that produced the ticket's genesis CREATE event (cli/mcp/python/jira/import). A legacy CREATE that carried no channel projects the projection-only fallback `unknown`. Immutable once set — an EDIT can never overwrite it. Distinct from actor/environment/source_* provenance: those record WHO/WHERE, this records WHICH INTERFACE.

creation_channel_inferred.description: Marks a `creation_channel` that was INFERRED for a legacy CREATE (a later story's concern) rather than recorded at genesis. Present (always `true`) only when inference ran; absent on tickets whose channel was stamped at CREATE.

detected_by.description: Detection channel that found this ticket (ticket d3ed). Set at CREATE time from the REBAR_DETECTED_BY env var or --detected-by CLI flag; absent when neither was provided.

close_class.description: The bounded classification recorded when a ticket is closed with `--class <value>` — REQUIRED on a `bug` close, and accepted on non-bug closes only for the administrative dispositions (`duplicate`/`obsolete`/`superseded`/`wontfix`). Folded onto the `*->closed` edge into reduced state so `rebar show <id>` surfaces WHY the ticket closed. Present only on closed tickets that recorded a class.

close_reason.description: The operator's stated justification for a reason-only administrative close (`--class obsolete` or `--class wontfix`, which REQUIRE `--reason=<text>`). Written onto the `*->closed` STATUS event in the same locked write as the close, folded here, and signed into the disposition attestation's manifest. Distinct from `force_close_reason`: this records why a truthful disposition closed, that one records why a gate was bypassed. Present only when a non-force close carried a reason.

force_close_reason.description: The operator's reason from `--force=<reason>` when a close bypassed its gates. Written onto the `*->closed` STATUS event in the same locked write as the close and folded here, so the justification for a bypass survives without depending on the second lock acquisition the best-effort FORCE_CLOSE audit comment needs (bug defiant-orthoclase-buck). Present only on a force-closed ticket; absence means the close was not forced.
